question: Compliance of agricultural price formation with Articles 39 and 40 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union

Article 39 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) establishes among the objectives of the common agricultural policy (CAP) the need to ensure a fair standard of living for the agricultural community, by increasing the individual earnings of farmers and ensuring reasonable prices.

Article 40 TFEU provides for the common organisation of agricultural markets to include measures concerning the regulation of prices and sets out that any common price policy is to be based on common criteria and uniform methods of calculation. However, significant differences exist in the way production costs, prices and margins are calculated across Member States.
This gives rise to situations in which farmers are required to sell agricultural products at prices below their costs of production. 1.

Does the Commission consider that the current EU framework for agricultural price formation and market organisation complies fully with the objectives of the CAP as set out in Articles 39 and 40 TFEU, particularly where agricultural products are systematically traded below the cost of production?

Does the Commission consider that additional EU-level measures are necessary to ensure the use of common criteria and uniform methodologies for calculating production costs and producer prices, and to better ensure that the objectives of a fair standard of living for farmers and market stabilisation, as set out in Article 39 TFEU, are achieved?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) 1. The Common Market Organisation (CMO) Regulation1 and the Unfair Trading Practices (UTP) Directive2 provide important tools to achieve the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) objective of ensuring a fair standard of living for the agricultural community while preserving the market orientation of the CAP.

The CMO Regulation was recently amended to strengthen farmers’ position in the chain3, including by better integrating elements of production costs into contractual price negotiations. In line with the Vision for Agriculture and Food4, the Commission will revise the UTP Directive with a view to addressing the issue of farmers being forced to systematically sell below their production costs. 2.

In this context, the EU Agri-food Chain Observatory (AFCO)5 seeks to develop a shared understanding of the functioning of the food supply chain and to increase transparency regarding prices, cost structures and the distribution of margins and added value. It does so by bringing together Member States and actors active along the supply chain.

The organisation of the supply chain varies across sectors and product types, with agri-food market structures also differing between Member States. These differences require a careful analysis before any additional measures are taken at national or EU level.
1 Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 December 2013

establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products and repealing Council Regulations (EEC) No 922/72, (EEC) No 234/79, (EC) No 1037/2001 and (EC) No 1234/2007, OJ L 347, 20.12.2013, pp. 671.

2 Directive (EU) 2019/633 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on unfair trading practices in business-to-business relationships in the agricultural and food supply chain, OJ L 111, 25.4.2019, pp. 59.

3 Regulation (EU) 2026/1739 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) No 1308/2013, (EU) 2021/2115 and (EU) 2021/2116 as regards the strengthening of the position of farmers in the food supply chain, OJ L, 2026/1739, 29.7.2026. http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1739/oj.

4 Commission’s Communication, A Vision for Agriculture and Food Shaping together an attractive farming and agri-food sector for future generations, COM/2025/75 final. 5 https://agriculture.ec.europa.eu/common-agricultural-policy/agri-food-supply-chain/afco_en.
